chapters.title: 1. Introduction to HTML5
chapters.content:
HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the most basic building block of the Web. It defines the meaning and structure of web content. Other technologies besides HTML are generally used to describe a web page's appearance/presentation (CSS) or functionality/behavior (JavaScript).

The Boilerplate Structure

Every HTML5 document requires a standard 'boilerplate' structure.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>My First Webpage</title>
  </head>
  <body>
    <h1>Hello, World!</h1>
  </body>
</html>
Pro Tip: Viewport Meta Tag
The viewport meta tag is essential for responsive web design. It tells the browser how to control the page's dimensions and scaling on mobile devices.

chapters.title: 2. Document Structure
chapters.content:
HTML uses tags to structure content. The head contains metadata, while the body contains the visible content.

Headings & Paragraphs

Use <h1> through <h6> for headings and <p> for paragraphs. There should only be one <h1> per page for SEO and accessibility.

<h1>Main Heading</h1>
<h2>Subheading</h2>
<p>This is a paragraph of text.</p>

chapters.title: 3. Semantic Elements
chapters.content:
Semantic HTML5 elements clearly describe their meaning to both the browser and the developer. This is crucial for screen readers and SEO.

Core Semantic Tags

  • <header> - Intro content or navigation.
  • <nav> - Navigation links.
  • <main> - The main content of the document.
  • <article> - Independent, self-contained content.
  • <section> - A thematic grouping of content.
  • <footer> - Footer for its nearest sectioning content.
Why Semantic HTML?
It makes the web accessible to everyone and helps search engines understand the importance of content.

chapters.title: 4. Forms & Inputs
chapters.content:
Forms are how you collect user input. HTML5 introduced several new input types.

Basic Form

<form action="/submit" method="POST">
  <label for="email">Email:</label>
  <input type="email" id="email" required>
  <button type="submit">Send</button>
</form>

Notice the type="email" and required attributes—these are built-in HTML5 validation features.

chapters.title: 5. Multimedia (Audio/Video)
chapters.content:
Before HTML5, playing audio and video on a webpage required plugins like Flash. HTML5 introduced native multimedia elements.

The Video Element

<video width="320" height="240" controls>
  <source src="movie.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  Your browser does not support the video tag.
</video>
Responsive Videos
To make videos responsive, you can omit the width/height attributes and use CSS: max-width: 100%; height: auto;

chapters.title: 6. HTML5 Canvas API
chapters.content:
The <canvas> element is used to draw graphics on a web page via JavaScript.

Basic Canvas Usage

First, define the canvas in HTML:

<canvas id="myCanvas" width="200" height="100"></canvas>

Then, use Javascript to draw on it:

const c = document.getElementById("myCanvas");
const ctx = c.getContext("2d");
ctx.fillStyle = "#04AA6D";
ctx.fillRect(0, 0, 150, 75);

This concludes the HTML5 course. You are now ready to style your documents with CSS3!
